questions.prompt: How many expressions are in the header of a standard for loop?
questions.explanation: A standard for loop header contains three expressions separated by semicolons: initialization, condition, and iterator.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: for (_____ i = 0; i < 5; i++) { Console.WriteLine(i); }
Arrange the for loop header parts in execution order.
Which part of the for loop header runs first?
questions.explanation: The initialization expression runs once before the first condition check.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: for (int i = 0; _____ i < 10; i++) { ... }
Write a for loop that calculates the sum of integers from 1 to 5 and prints the result.
What happens if the condition expression is omitted from a for loop?
questions.explanation: Omitting the condition is equivalent to true, creating an infinite loop unless a break is used.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: for (int i = 0; i < 5; _____++) { ... }
Arrange the complete for loop syntax in order.
Can you omit the iterator expression from a for loop?
options: Yes, but you must update inside the body
Only if the body is empty
questions.explanation: The iterator is optional. If omitted, you must manually update the loop variable inside the body to avoid an infinite loop.
